discovery: Ultrapure hexagonal boron nitride crystals and their use to build high-quality van der Waals heterostructures

nominees.name: Takashi Taniguchi
nominees.affiliation: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), Tsukuba, Japan

nominees.name: Kenji Watanabe
nominees.affiliation: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), Tsukuba, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and van der Waals heterostructures
motivation: Taniguchi and Watanabe developed high-pressure growth of exceptionally pure hexagonal boron nitride crystals. Philip Kim and collaborators showed that hBN, used as an atomically flat dielectric substrate and encapsulant, gives graphene and other 2D crystals mobilities and clean conditions never reached before. Together these advances turned atomic layers into a designable materials platform. Stacked van der Waals heterostructures have since revealed the fractional quantum Hall effect and Hofstadter's butterfly in graphene, magic-angle superconductivity and correlated insulators, intrinsic 2D magnetism, and fractional Chern insulators without a magnetic field. Thousands of laboratories worldwide depend on NIMS crystals, and few recent experimental discoveries in quantum materials would have been possible without this combination of crystal growth and device engineering. It is a clear case of patient materials craftsmanship opening an entire field of emergent physics.
